This petition was called on for hearing today.

CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE DIPANKAR DATTA  2  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRASHANT KUMAR MISHRA For Petitioner(s) Mr. Harmeet Singh Ruprah, AOR For Respondent(s)
 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1.
Delay condoned.

2. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh dated 14th December,
2023 requires the concerned Land Acquisition Officer, on a remand being ordered, to decide compensation payable to the respondents in the light of the Guidelines issued by the State Government and also by taking into consideration Clause 4.3 of the Guidelines issued by the Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India.

entities.text: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioning Corporation vehemently argues that the circular dated 26th October, 2015 issued by the Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development cannot be construed to be an order of the Central Government within the meaning of Section 113 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereafter the 2013 Act); also, such circular has since been withdrawn Divisional Manager M.P. 2 by the Central Government itself.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, therefore, contended that the High Court was in error in ordering a remand.

4. Assuming that the circular dated 26 th October, 2015 is not an order issued by the Central Government within the meaning of Section 113 of the 2013 Act and/or that the same stands withdrawn, nothing much turns on it.

5. In the present case, land acquisition proceedings commenced with the publication of the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter 1894 Act) on 16th September, 2011.
The award was passed by the Land Acquisition Officer on 24th April, 2015, much after the 2013 Act was enforced w.e.f. 1st January, 2014.

The High Court found that compensation was determined by the Land Acquisition Officer in accordance with the principles laid down in the 1894 Act, though the circular dated 26 th October, 2015 ordained determination of compensation in the manner provided by the 2013 Act.

6. True it is, the order of remand has been passed by the High Court based on its impression that the circular dated 26th October, 2015 is indeed an order within the meaning of Section 113 of the 2013 Act.
However, as observed above, the circular is not too relevant.

We are inclined to hold that the High Court could have reached the same conclusion it ultimately did bearing in mind the provisions contained in Section 24(1) of the 2013 Act read with Section 26 thereof.
7. We see no reason to hold that the High Court erred in ordering a remand and, accordingly, are not inclined to entertain the special leave petitions.
The same are, accordingly, dismissed.
8. The Land Acquisition Officer, on remand, shall proceed to redetermine compensation in accordance with the provisions of the 2013 Act.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

(JATINDER KAUR) (SUDHIR KUMAR SHARMA)
P.S. to REGISTRAR COURT MASTER (NSH)
